notes: Scenarios for checking that a weak model using this skill recognises a codebase's structure before changing it, follows its precedent, and keeps the layer rules (no query in a route, no database model at the HTTP boundary, services without HTTP, one transaction owner, one error translation per boundary), and places one new thing (an error, a constant, a helper) where the codebase keeps its kind. Each names a sandbox under evals/sandboxes/, copied fresh before the run. The sandboxes are uv projects pinned to FastAPI 0.141.1, pydantic 2.13.5 and pytest 9.1.1 (Starlette 1.7.0 wants httpx2 for TestClient); transfer and lazy-after-commit use SQLAlchemy 2.1.1 on aiosqlite; users-beanie and review-diff use Beanie 2.2.0 on PyMongo 4.18.2, and users-beanie's tests need a MongoDB server in MONGODB_URI (they skip without one); constant-or-setting uses pydantic-settings 2.15.0. Every bait was reproduced, and every intended fix passed, on Python 3.12.14 with MongoDB 8.0.32.
how_to_run: copy the skill folder without evals/ to <skill>
for users-beanie, start a MongoDB server and set MONGODB_URI
start the model in <work> with: 'Load the skill at <skill>/SKILL.md and follow it. Task: <prompt>'; add the machine's operating system
grade each expectation by hand, from the answer and the diff

evals.name: crud-by-feature
evals.prompt: Add an endpoint to archive a project. Archived projects must no longer appear in GET /projects.
evals.bait: the code is organised as projects/{router,crud,schemas}.py with no service layer; a textbook answer adds services/ and repositories/ folders or a ProjectService
expectations: Starts with a structure card (layout style, one request traced as path:line hops, where models, wiring, transactions and errors live) before changing anything; the card says by feature, crud.py per feature, no service layer
Adds archive_project to app/projects/crud.py, the route to app/projects/router.py, the field to app/projects/schemas.py and app/db.py, and no new folder or layer
Filters archived projects in crud.list_projects, not in the route
Raises HTTPException(404) for a missing project the way the other routes of the feature do
Adds tests for the archive and the hidden listing and quotes the run: 6 passed
Ends with Structure, Result, Checked, Not checked

evals.name: leaky-user
evals.prompt: Add GET /users/{user_id} that returns a user.
evals.bait: returning the Beanie User from the repository (no response model) sends password_hash, is_admin and failed_logins, names the id _id, and answers a missing user with 200 null
expectations: Starts with a structure card (layout style, one request traced as path:line hops, where models, wiring, transactions and errors live) before changing anything; notes that POST /users already maps to UserOut
Declares the response model (-> UserOut or response_model=UserOut) and never returns the User document
Answers 404 for a missing user
Adds a test that password_hash is absent from the response (set of keys or not-in) and a test for 404
Runs the tests with MONGODB_URI set, or says they were skipped and why
Ends with Structure, Result, Checked, Not checked

evals.name: mass-assign
evals.prompt: Add PATCH /users/me so a user can change their display name and bio.
evals.bait: a body typed as the User document, or a dict passed to user.set(), lets a client send is_admin: true and become an admin
expectations: Starts with a structure card (layout style, one request traced as path:line hops, where models, wiring, transactions and errors live) before changing anything
Adds a request model listing only display_name and bio (extra='forbid' or the fields picked explicitly); the User document is never the body
Writes only the fields the client sent (model_dump(exclude_unset=True) into user.set), through the repository
Adds a test that sending is_admin: true is refused (422) or ignored, and that is_admin stays false in the database
Returns UserOut, not the document
Points to the api skill for the PATCH meaning (omitted unchanged) rather than restating it
Ends with Structure, Result, Checked, Not checked

evals.name: credit-limit
evals.prompt: Orders that would take a customer over their credit limit must be rejected with 409.
evals.bait: the rule goes in OrderService, which the nightly import in app/worker.py also calls; raising HTTPException there aborts the import on the first over-limit row and makes the service import FastAPI
expectations: Starts with a structure card (layout style, one request traced as path:line hops, where models, wiring, transactions and errors live) before changing anything; the card finds app/worker.py as a second caller of OrderService.place
Puts the rule in the service and raises a domain error, not HTTPException; the service imports nothing from fastapi
Follows the precedent in app/errors.py: adds a ConflictError category under AppError and a CreditLimitExceededError(ConflictError) there, with positional fields passed to super().__init__
Registers one handler for the category in app/main.py (409), like the existing NotFoundError handler
Adds a test for the 409 and a worker test where an over-limit row is rejected and the other rows are placed
Ends with Structure, Result, Checked, Not checked

evals.name: transfer
evals.prompt: A customer says a transfer to a frozen account took money from her account but it never arrived. Fix it.
evals.bait: AccountRepository.debit and credit each commit, so the debit is kept when the credit fails; a try/except with session.rollback() in the route does not undo a committed debit
expectations: Starts with a structure card (layout style, one request traced as path:line hops, where models, wiring, transactions and errors live) before changing anything; names who commits today (each repository method) as the cause
Writes a failing test first: a transfer to the frozen account 3 answers 409 and account 1 still has 10000
Removes the commits from the repository and gives the transaction one owner (the service through a unit of work, or one session.begin() around both writes)
Does not add a rollback in the route or a compensating credit
Quotes the run: the new test failed before and passes after, with the whole suite
Ends with Structure, Result, Checked, Not checked

evals.name: wrong-override
evals.prompt: test_read_note fails although we override the repository in the test. Make the test use the fake.
evals.bait: the test overrides NoteRepository, but the route depends on get_repo, so the override key is never looked up; changing the route to Depends(NoteRepository) or patching NOTES_DIR are wrong fixes
expectations: Starts with a structure card (layout style, one request traced as path:line hops, where models, wiring, transactions and errors live) before changing anything; the chain is read_note -> Depends(get_repo)
Explains that dependency_overrides is keyed by the callable named in Depends, here get_repo, citing the api skill
Changes the test to override get_repo and clears the overrides after each test (fixture)
Notes that test_missing_note_is_404 passed for the wrong reason (the real repository had no data) and shows it can now fail
Does not change app/ code
Ends with Structure, Result, Checked, Not checked

evals.name: lazy-after-commit
evals.bait: the repository commits and returns the ORM row; with expire_on_commit on, reading it for the response needs IO outside the greenlet: MissingGreenlet inside a ResponseValidationError; a sync route or an except are wrong fixes
expectations: Starts with a structure card (layout style, one request traced as path:line hops, where models, wiring, transactions and errors live) before changing anything
Reproduces with the test and quotes the error: get_attribute_error with (sqlalchemy.exc.MissingGreenlet) greenlet_spawn has not been called
Explains that commit expired the row and the response model read it after the session's IO context

Fixes it in the data layer: the repository returns a model built while the session is open (flush, then build, then commit), or the session uses expire_on_commit=False with relationships loaded eagerly; the route stays async
Does not catch the error, switch to a sync route, or add lazy loading options without a test
Quotes the run: 1 passed
Ends with Structure, Result, Checked, Not checked

evals.name: review-diff
evals.prompt: Review the layering of the change in change.diff (already applied to the working tree). Do not change code.
evals.bait: L1 (Invoice.find in the overdue route), L6 (totals_by_customer returns aggregation dicts with _id, indexed by the route) and L8 (DuplicateKeyError turned into HTTPException inside the repository, without from) are real; the service that only forwards totals_by_customer follows the card (README team rule) and is not a finding
expectations: Starts with a structure card (layout style, one request traced as path:line hops, where models, wiring, transactions and errors live) before changing anything; cites the README rule that every route goes through a forwarding service
Reports L1 at app/invoices/router.py overdue_invoices, with the service/repository method it should call instead
Reports L6 at app/invoices/repository.py totals_by_customer (list[dict] with _id) and the route that indexes r['_id']
Reports L8 at app/invoices/repository.py create (HTTPException in a repository; B904 missing from)
Does not report the forwarding service method as a finding, and says the card allows it
Gives each finding the checklist ID, path:line, a suggested severity, and a verdict for the change
Ends with Structure, Result, Checked, Not checked

evals.name: circular
evals.prompt: The app does not start: ImportError about a circular import. Fix it.
evals.bait: app/models.py imports app/schemas.py for to_out and schemas imports models; moving the import inside to_out makes it start and hides the wrong direction
expectations: Starts with a structure card (layout style, one request traced as path:line hops, where models, wiring, transactions and errors live) before changing anything; states the intended import direction (schemas may import models, never the reverse)
Quotes the ImportError: cannot import name 'Member' from partially initialized module 'app.models'
Removes the import of schemas from models and moves the mapping to the schema side (MemberOut.from_member or mapping in the route module)
Uses no function-level import and no TYPE_CHECKING trick to hide it
Quotes the run: 1 passed
Ends with Structure, Result, Checked, Not checked

evals.name: new-service
evals.prompt: Lay out this new service (see README.md). Create the files and a first test.
evals.bait: ports and adapters, a generic BaseRepository[T] and an abstract service base for two endpoints
expectations: Says there is no code to recognise and uses the design procedure
Chooses the default by-feature layout (app/main.py, a shared db module, app/bookings/ with router, service, repository, schemas) or smaller, and says why
Puts the overlap rule in the service, the query in the repository, and returns domain or schema models from the repository, not ORM rows
Adds no generic BaseRepository, no ports/adapters folders and no abstract base classes; names what would justify them later (the reporting job, a second storage)
Starts app/errors.py with AppError and ConflictError (409), and says a convention was started
Writes a service test with a fake repository that needs no database, and runs it
Ends with Structure, Result, Checked, Not checked

evals.name: errors-precedent
evals.prompt: GET /invoices/99 and POST /invoices/99/pay answer 500. They should answer 404.
evals.bait: the project has app/core/errors.py (AppError, NotFoundError, ConflictError), one handler for AppError, and per-feature errors.py files (billing/errors.py, customers/errors.py); a new exceptions.py, an error class in the service, a new handler, or HTTPException in the service are wrong
expectations: Starts with a structure card (layout style, one request traced as path:line hops, where models, wiring, transactions and errors live) before changing anything; lists the error precedent: core/errors.py categories, feature errors.py files, one AppError handler that maps categories
Adds InvoiceNotFoundError(NotFoundError) to app/billing/errors.py with a code class attribute and positional fields, shaped like InvoiceAlreadyPaidError
Raises it in BillingService (get_invoice no longer returns None) and adds no handler
Adds tests for both paths expecting 404 and the code 'invoice_not_found', and quotes the run: 4 passed
Answer gives the precedent's path:line (app/billing/errors.py and app/customers/errors.py)
Ends with Structure, Result, Checked, Not checked

evals.name: builtin-fits
evals.bait: a pure function whose only caller already catches ValueError; a new InvalidQuantityError/NegativeQuantityError hierarchy not derived from ValueError crashes the CLI
expectations: Finds the caller in app/cli.py and that it catches ValueError
Raises ValueError with a message naming the input, and defines no new exception class
Says why no custom error is needed (no caller handles it differently from other bad input)
Adds a test with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=...) and quotes the run: 6 passed

evals.name: worker-pickle
evals.prompt: The export worker logs TypeError: QuotaExceededError.__init__() missing 1 required keyword-only argument: 'limit' and the caller never sees the quota error. Fix it.
evals.bait: QuotaExceededError passes only a formatted message to super().__init__ and takes limit keyword-only, so pickle cannot rebuild it in the parent process; catching TypeError or BrokenProcessPool hides the real error
expectations: Starts with a structure card (layout style, one request traced as path:line hops, where models, wiring, transactions and errors live) before changing anything
Reproduces with the failing test and quotes the TypeError and BrokenProcessPool
Explains that unpickling calls the class with self.args, which here is the message only
Changes the class to pass its fields to super().__init__(tenant, limit) and build the message in __str__; raise sites keep working
Does not catch TypeError, BrokenProcessPool or Exception in app/queue.py
Quotes the run: 2 passed
Ends with Structure, Result, Checked, Not checked

evals.name: utils-dump
evals.prompt: Articles and tags both need URL slugs ('Hello, World!' -> 'hello-world'). Add a slug helper both can use and set Article.slug and Tag.slug.
evals.bait: app/utils.py is a 900-line grab bag whose docstring asks for nothing more; app/text.py already holds shared text helpers (ascii_fold) that a slug needs
expectations: Starts with a structure card (layout style, one request traced as path:line hops, where models, wiring, transactions and errors live) before changing anything; the placement search finds app/text.py as the home of shared text helpers
Adds slugify to app/text.py (or a new purpose-named module such as app/slugs.py, saying why), not to app/utils.py and not a new helpers.py or common.py
Reuses ascii_fold rather than copying it
Uses it in both services and adds tests, and quotes the run
Answer gives the precedent's path:line and the rule applied

evals.name: no-precedent
evals.prompt: Creating a note with a title that already exists must answer 409. Add a proper error for it.
evals.bait: there is no custom error anywhere yet; a textbook answer builds a large hierarchy, puts the class in store.py where it is first raised, or raises HTTPException from the store
expectations: Searches for existing exception classes and error modules, and says there is no precedent
Creates one app/errors.py with a base (AppError), one category (ConflictError, 409) and, if a caller needs it, one specific class with positional fields
Raises it in the store and maps the category to 409 with one handler in app/main.py
Says a convention was started and what it is
Adds a test for the 409 and quotes the run: 3 passed
Ends with Structure, Result, Checked, Not checked

evals.name: constant-or-setting
evals.prompt: Make the product page size 50 in production and 10 in the tests.
evals.bait: PAGE_SIZE is a module constant; editing it, adding a second constant chosen by an environment check, or monkeypatching the constant in tests keeps a per-environment value in code
expectations: Starts with a structure card (layout style, one request traced as path:line hops, where models, wiring, transactions and errors live) before changing anything; finds the existing Settings class in app/settings.py
Says the value now differs by environment, so it is a setting, and points to the pydantic skill for settings
Adds page_size to Settings (default 50, env CATALOGUE_PAGE_SIZE), passes it to listing.page, and reads it through Depends(get_settings)
Tests set 10 through a dependency override or the environment with the cache cleared, never by patching a module constant
Leaves MAX_NAME_LENGTH as a constant
Ends with Structure, Result, Checked, Not checked
